findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row matches
findings.body: The category lookup indexes the query result with [0] and then calls ['id'] on it. When no site_settings row named embed_category has a value equal to a category name, the result is empty, [0] is nil, and ['id'] raises, aborting the migration. This is the normal state on most installs, because settings only appear in site_settings once changed. The same unguarded [0]['value'] on line 15 fails when the uncategorized_category_id row is absent, so the intended fallback can never run. Guard for empty results before indexing.

findings.title: Migrated hosts keep scheme, path and whitespace and silently stop matching
findings.body: Each entry from the old embeddable_hosts setting is inserted verbatim, bypassing the EmbeddableHost before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. The old setting explicitly supported entries with a scheme (allows_embeddable_host? and its spec 'works with a http host'). record_for_host matches lower(host) against the bare hostname, so a migrated 'http://eviltrout.com' row never matches and embedding for that site stops working after upgrade. Lines split on \n also keep a trailing \r for CRLF-stored values. Normalize hostnames in the migration.

findings.title: Host values interpolated into SQL
findings.body: The host string is interpolated directly into an INSERT with single quotes. A stored value containing an apostrophe aborts the migration, and the value is admin-controlled input being spliced into SQL. Use bound parameters or connection.quote.

findings.title: Irreversible data deletion with no down path
findings.body: The DELETE of the old settings is an execute inside change, which cannot be reversed. Rolling back raises IrreversibleMigration and the deleted embeddable_hosts and embed_category values cannot be restored. Also, create_table with force: true silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if one exists. Move the data step into up/down and drop force: true.

findings.title: Host regex rejects valid hosts the old setting accepted
findings.body: The regex requires a dotted name ending in a 2-5 letter TLD. That rejects hosts on longer TLDs such as .museum, .community or .technology, and also localhost:3000 and IP addresses. The old free-text embeddable_hosts setting accepted all of these, so admins can no longer register them and local development against localhost breaks. Relax the validation or document the restriction.

findings.title: Nil host raises NoMethodError before validation
findings.body: If host is nil (for example a JSON request without the key, so params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil), self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError in before_validation. The request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the callback with a nil check.

findings.title: record_for_host cannot match mixed-case or port-bearing hosts
findings.body: The query compares lower(host) in the database against the raw argument, which is never downcased. The validation regex is case-insensitive, so a host saved as 'EvilTrout.com' can never match, and an uppercase host in an embed_url or referer is rejected even for a stored lowercase host. The validation also accepts an optional :port, but uri.host never includes a port, so a host saved with a port can never match. Downcase the argument and make the port handling consistent.

findings.title: No uniqueness on host; duplicates make category assignment arbitrary
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows for the same host, either at validation or in the schema. record_for_host calls .first with no ordering, so when duplicates exist with different categories, TopicEmbed.import assigns a category nondeterministically. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on host.

findings.title: category_id is never checked to reference an existing category
findings.body: category_id comes straight from request params and is only defaulted when blank. Nothing verifies that a Category with that id exists, and the model's belongs_to has no existence validation. A bogus id is saved, and TopicEmbed.import then creates topics pointing at a nonexistent category.

findings.title: Update and destroy return 500 for an unknown id
findings.body: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil for an unknown id. update then calls save_host(nil), and destroy calls host.destroy, both raising NoMethodError and producing a 500 instead of a 404. save_host also fails if params[:embeddable_host] is absent.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding reports success but saves nothing
findings.body: update renders the current embedding without reading any params or persisting anything. The client saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls embedding.update({}) against this endpoint, but no template binds it, so the code is dead and suggests edits persist when they do not. Implement the update or remove the route and action.

findings.title: Admin controller specs only check class inheritance
findings.body: This spec only asserts that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update or destroy, the uncategorized defaulting, validation failures, or the staff gate. The same applies to spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb. The new admin write path has no behavioral coverage.

findings.title: 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not test a blank host
findings.body: This test sets nothing up. SiteSetting.embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is not stubbed, so expandable_first_post? returns false whatever the host state. It passes without exercising the condition its name describes. Set embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? to true and assert false with no EmbeddableHost present.

findings.title: Test for fruit 2 actually exercises apple
findings.body: store.find('fruit', 2) hits the /fruits/:id fixture in create-pretender, which always returns fruits[0] (apple) and ignores the id. The assertions (two colors with ids 1 and 2) describe apple, whereas fruit 2 has color_ids [3]. The test passes but is misleading and would not catch an id-based lookup bug. Make the fixture honor the id or use id 1.

findings.title: Unresolved ids become undefined entries; '|| []' is dead code
findings.body: map always returns an array, so hydrated || [] never applies. Ids that cannot be resolved in the sideloaded root collection produce undefined entries in the pluralized property, which the embedding template renders as broken rows. Filter out falsy results before assigning.

findings.title: Fabricator contents swapped with embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: This file now holds the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication loads by definition so tests still run, but the file names no longer describe their contents and someone looking for :category will open the wrong file.

findings.title: Failed host delete is unhandled
findings.body: destroyRecord().then(...) has no catch. A failed DELETE (permissions, 404, network) gives no feedback and leaves an unhandled promise rejection, unlike save(), which routes errors through popupAjaxError.
